Windows release contract

The visible application name is PMA Mic Bridge. Package filenames, executable
name, installation ID and settings paths stay stable for existing installations.

1. Set Version in ApolloMicBridge.csproj manually to the next numeric version.
   Commit and push the change to main. Ordinary main pushes and pull requests
   build and test packages; they do not change versions or publish releases.
   Optionally add customer notes in .github/release-notes/<version>.txt. GitHub
   generates commit/PR notes automatically and prepends this file when present.
2. After the main build passes, create and push a matching numeric tag without v:
   git tag 0.2.0
   git push origin 0.2.0
   Use increasing versions and tag the intended main commit. Existing tags must
   never be moved or deleted. The tag must exactly match the project Version.
3. The tag pipeline runs the audio/settings/updater checks, builds packages,
   and verifies installer, uninstaller and portable update behavior. Only after
   all checks pass does a separate job create a draft and attach these assets:
   ApolloMicBridge-Setup-<version>.exe
   ApolloMicBridge-Portable-win-x64.zip
   Each package also has a matching .sha256 file. The pipeline compares GitHub's
   asset sizes and SHA-256 digests to the tested local files before publishing
   a stable release. A failed upload leaves a draft; retrying completes it.
   A retry of an already published release preserves its assets and notes.
   Tag runs are not cancelled by a newer push. Pull requests have read access;
   only the release job has write access through the built-in GitHub token.

Keep the portable ZIP's three root files unchanged: ApolloMicBridge.exe,
LICENSE and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt. Package names must remain compatible with
the updater. Local build.ps1 uses the same project version for the app and setup.

The updater also accepts manually published prereleases, including tags such
as v0.3.0-beta.1. The automated pipeline uses numeric stable tags only.

The app checks the 100 most recent published releases once per launch and on
request. It chooses the highest version above its assembly version. Missing
assets, missing checksums and network/rate-limit failures are shown separately
from the audio status. There is no GitHub token in the application.

Installing an offered update downloads and verifies the package first, then
stops audio, saves its settings and starts a separate copy of the application
to perform the update. Setup installations use their existing per-user path;
portable installations replace only their three package files and roll back on
replacement failure. The updater restarts the app and resumes a previously
running microphone route. Autostart registration and settings are preserved.

The helper and installer log are retained in the application's local Update
directory and reused on the next update. Downloads and portable backups are
removed after success. A failed portable rollback retains its backup for recovery.

Versions before 0.2.0 do not have an updater. Install 0.2.0 once manually to
receive subsequent releases through the app.
